name: room
text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline. It sharpens fine details in still frames better than generic upscalers, giving us a measurable quality bump without extra compute. Trade-off: it adds one extra step to the workflow, but the gain in clarity outweighs the minor slowdown.

name: Torque
text: Depth-aware upscaling won’t fix EXCAVA’s motion blur—it’s a temporal artifact, not a spatial one. The real risk is wasting effort on a tool that targets the wrong problem. VFI-Flow’s 20-30% compute hit is a gamble, but it directly attacks the temporal bottleneck; test it first on a 10-second clip with measurable blur metrics before committing.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add VFI-Flow to EXCAVA’s motion pipeline. It reconstructs motion blur into sharp frames, directly attacking the temporal bottleneck that depth-aware upscaling can’t touch. The trade-off is a 20-30% compute hit, but the gain in motion clarity outweighs the slowdown—test it first on a 10-second clip with the lead’s approval.

name: Torque
text: VFI-Flow’s compute hit isn’t just a gamble—it’s a potential dead end if EXCAVA’s motion blur stems from camera shake or rolling shutter, not frame interpolation. Test a rolling-shutter correction tool like RSDeBlur first on the same 10-second clip; if it clears motion blur without the compute penalty, VFI-Flow’s 20-30% hit is wasted effort.

name: Dynamo
text:
DECISION: Run VFI-Flow only on keyframes with worst motion blur, then let EXCAVA handle the rest—if RSDeBlur clears blur on the 10-second test clip without compute penalty, swap it in instead.

Result: A 0.5%+ quality gain in motion clarity with minimal compute waste.
